translation_notes: 163-region case: the graph reaches the function only through `with locked_graph() as g:` (never a parameter, never returned), and locked_graph/_class/_mint_hash_iri/_ensure_type_with_label/_is_abs_iri/_list_species_summaries are module-level helpers defined elsewhere in the source file. Restored via context_shim.py, same family as the sibling add_isolated/..._add_atomic_weight_to_element (same repo, same helper set): _mint_hash_iri made deterministic and call-scoped (counter resets each locked_graph() entry) instead of hashing datetime.now(), so the two mints of 'WeightPercentage' within one call (calculated/experimental branches) still mint distinct nodes and both sides mint the identical sequence for the identical call.

the stratum's construction: `exists = any(g.triples((species_ref, RDF.type, _class(OS, "Species"))))` -> `exists = bool(m{ {species_ref} rdf:type {_class(OS, "Species")} }(g))`. Only rdf: gets a @prefix (RDF.type is the only rdflib.namespace name the region body itself references; RDFS/XSD are only used inside the out-of-region helpers, restored via context_shim, matching the sibling's precedent of not prefixing what the region body never spells).

the four g.add(...) calls each become +{ }(g), call-suffix form (no @graph needed: each is the only write to g on its line/branch). The three g.set(...) calls are LEFT AS rdflib API, same reasoning and same precedent as the sibling: .set() first removes any existing (s,p,*) triple before adding, a replace-then-add that +{ } (add-only) does not cover -- behaviourally identical here only because each node is freshly minted (no prior value could exist to replace), which is an accident of the call site, not a property of +{ }.

_class(OS, "X") calls are left as plain Python (not rewritten to os:X), matching the sibling's precedent for this same repo/helper family, since _class is a real project helper the shim restores rather than an artefact of extraction.

run_pair's entry=/calls= comparison only looks at return value + arguments -- the region returns only str(ea)/an error string, never the graph -- so, following the sibling's precedent, driver.py bypasses run_pair and drives both sides by hand, snapshotting context_shim.LAST_GRAPH right after each call and comparing by isomorphism, calls never overlapping. Unlike the sibling, this region READS before it writes (the exists check), so the graph must arrive pre-populated: fixture.ttl's triples are replayed into context_shim.SEED before every call.

fixture.ttl covers two os:Species (several solutions), a same-shaped os:Element neighbour (must not satisfy the check), and the zero-solution case via a species IRI absent from the fixture. Five driver cases exercise: exists=True with the calculated branch, exists=True with the experimental+molecular-formula branches, exists=False (catalog-error return, no spurious triple), missing species_iri/data_label, and a non-absolute species_iri.
